description: The provided image is a circular, multi-layered pie chart illustrating the structure of medical ethics principles as applied in the MedEthicsQA benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs). At the center, four primary ethical pillars are displayed: “Beneficence” (large blue segment), “Justice” (orange), “Non-Maleficence” (purple), and “Autonomy” (green), each occupying a distinct quadrant. Radiating outward from each of these core principles are multiple sub-principles or ethical obligations, each labeled with a specific ethical directive. For example, under “Beneficence,” sub-principles include “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patient,” and “Ethical Research.” Under “Justice,” directives include “Promote the Health of Community,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally.” The “Non-Maleficence” section includes “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” The “Autonomy” segment lists “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed,” and “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication.” The chart visually organizes these ethical components hierarchically, with the central principles forming the foundation and the outer segments detailing their practical applications. The color-coding and radial layout emphasize the relationship between overarching principles and their specific ethical imperatives, serving as a conceptual map for evaluating LLMs’ understanding of medical ethics as defined in the MedEthicsQA framework.
